name: Woomera Range Complex
tagline: Australia's first satellite, WRESAT (1967), and Britain's Black Arrow launch of Prospero (1971)
description: Woomera is a rocket range in the South Australian desert, about 450 km north-west of Adelaide, set up in 1946-47 for the Anglo-Australian long-range weapons project. Two of its launch areas reached orbit. From Launch Area 8, a US Redstone with Sparta upper stages put WRESAT, a 45 kg satellite built by the Weapons Research Establishment, into a near-polar orbit on 29 November 1967: Australia's first satellite. From Launch Area 5B, a Black Arrow carried Prospero into orbit on 28 October 1971, the first British satellite launched on a British rocket; the programme was cancelled afterwards. The orbital launch areas are disused, but the range, now run by the RAAF, is still used for defence testing; its prohibited area covers 122,188 km2.
best_known_for: Australia's first satellite, WRESAT (1967), and Britain's Black Arrow launch of Prospero (1971)
